utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone in this courtroom. If there are no issues to be raised -- you never disappoint me, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you very much. There is a matter that we need to raise. It has to do -- representatives of the [redacted] that I am greeting here, I would like to specify that General Galic would like to say that himself and his country had the greatest respect for [redacted]and her government. Now, unfortunately, I have to say this without the representatives of the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am not sure that we are in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are not at this moment. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if it is about the presence of, let me say, our guests today, then we have to turn into closed session and if it is not about the testimony itself, but about other issues, I have to ask the representatives or guests of today perhaps to leave the courtroom for a second so that you can raise the issue. And at the same time, I would then turn into closed session. [Interpretation] Could I ask you please to leave the courtroom for a minute or two? [In English] I have confirmed in my screen that we are in closed session now, please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will then now turn into open session. Yes, we are in open session now. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. In relation to the time table for the rest of the week, there are some difficulties. Unlike last week, this week we have a surfeit of evidence. On Friday we have General Van Baal and it is important that his evidence does indeed commence on Friday morning because we have some specially arranged interpreters in the Dutch language. I have in mind that if his evidence is not completed on that day, then we will arrange a day further, later in the Prosecution case, for it to be completed. We will bring him back, probably towards the end of June or the last -- the first week in July. Mr. President, on Thursday, coming back a day, we have David Harland and as I explained last week there are some pressing and unavoidable personal reasons pertaining to him, which really require that his evidence also commences on 9.00 on Thursday morning. He would not be able beyond Thursday for some time. I am hopeful that we can finish his evidence on Thursday. That brings us back to tomorrow. It is now abundantly clear that there is no prospect of Mr. Turner being reached. Indeed, there is every prospect that tomorrow would be insufficient to finish Richard Mole and Witness W. I, therefore, propose that we finish Witness W and in any remaining time we continue with Richard Mole, but then Richard Mole would have to go over to a later date. At least he is coming from an almost neighbouring state, the United Kingdom, and relatively speaking, there would be less disruption and cost then if he was coming from further afield. So, Mr. President, perhaps I should sit down at this point and just having made those observations, inquiries whether that is acceptable to the Trial Chamber and to my learned colleagues. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, first give you or Ms. Pilipovic the opportunity to respond.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am just looking at the schedule and the Defence is preparing itself according to the schedule received on the 31 of May. So considering the number of witnesses and the change in the schedule that we just heard from my learned colleague, the Defence will not be able to prepare itself for examination of Mr. Harland or Mr. Van Baal, particularly bearing in mind their statements which are quite voluminous and the materials attached to them, to both -- in relation to both Mr. Harland and Mr. Van Baal. Perhaps if we can be more efficient in preparing ourselves, perhaps we shouldn't resume with Mr. Mole, but maybe his examination should be moved to another date, in order to prepare ourselves for Mr. Harland and Mr. Van Baal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, may I ask you, Mr. Harland and Mr. Van Baal were scheduled for this week; that is, the 6th and the 7th of June. So I do not fully understand why since additional preparation for Mr. Tucker will not be necessary at this moment, why the Defence would not be prepared.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, bearing in mind the schedule, the Defence is preparing for Mr. Tucker and now we are being told that Mr. Tucker will not testify. As for Mr. Van Baal, we got the information on Friday. So the time that we have available for the Defence, particularly the material that is given to us every day, it will be a problematic. We were just now informed that Mr. Tucker will not be able to come. And Mr. Tucker's statement contains 32 pages and we have already started working on it, you see? So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would have to have had it finished so that you could further prepare for Thursday and Friday, Mr. Harland and Mr. Van Baal.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We are trying to -- I believe that the Defence is always prepared for examination and so far we have made considerable efforts, but I believe that this -- these changes in the schedule effect us a great deal, our preparation and our discussions with the General. [Trial Chamber confers

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will allow the Prosecution to proceed according to the schedule that was just indicated and takes into consideration that no new witnesses have been added to the schedule, but that one witness fell off. We will adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: be reconvened on Wednesday, the 5th day of June, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.
